name: security-xs-leaks-observability-review
intent: Cross-site state inference through a concrete browser observation channel
artifacts: Suspected sensitive binary state, attacker-observable load/timing/size signal, frame policy and browser isolation settings.
trace: Separate protected state from noise and from values already public to the observer. Resolve the precise request and browser event visible without reading a cross-origin body.
experiment: Use two owned accounts/states and a bounded randomized local comparison with a public control; preserve raw observations and uncertainty rather than extracting real-user state.
disproof: A single faster response or a same-origin debugger read is not a cross-site inference capability; unstable separation remains inconclusive.
repair: Retest the same observation channel after isolation/cache/response changes and verify legitimate clients still receive their own data.
branch_decisions: Randomize synthetic state order and record cache/service-worker warm-up and network variance. Distinguish an observable load/error event from reading its body. A consistent signal must identify protected state beyond public metadata; an automation-only timing or read channel is not available to an ordinary cross-origin page.
operational_method: Define the observation channel, bounded sample budget and decision rule before collecting timings. Randomize two synthetic private states, retain a public/no-state control and reserve a separate confirmation sequence so a threshold is not selected on the same noise it claims to distinguish. Report uncertainty when the separation does not persist; no real-user state extraction is needed.
